Splitting the nodes by the sign of their Fiedler vector entries cuts only that edge (accent): the negative side D, E, F (teal) and the non-negative side A, B, C (violet), returned as the id lists [4, 5, 6] and [1, 2, 3]." width="100%"} Spectral bisection divides the nodes into those with a negative Fiedler vector entry and those with a non-negative one (see `fiedler_vector()`). Because the Fiedler vector is the smoothest non-constant labelling of the graph, the split tends to cut few edges while keeping both sides reasonably balanced: it approximates the minimum ratio cut. Applied recursively it gives a simple hierarchical partitioning, and it is the classic first step of graph partitioning for parallel computing and image segmentation. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use the normalized Laplacian (approximating the normalized cut). Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[int], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(negative_side, non_negative_side)`, each a sorted list of node IDs. Matches NetworkX's `spectral_bisection()` up to the arbitrary sign of the Fiedler vector, which can swap the two sides. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, disconnected, has fewer than two nodes, or has a negative weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a bridge split along the bridge: ::: {#3720d7c3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEF")) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) left, right = graph.spectral_bisection() [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in left], [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in right] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['D', 'E', 'F'], ['A', 'B', 'C']) ``` ::: :::
